svg.title: Does the drying wear it out, or does time?
svg.desc: Two graphs of how well the moss comes back, side by side, for four sets of trays dried daily, weekly, monthly and never. On the left the horizontal axis is days since the experiment started, and the four lines are spread far apart, with the daily trays falling fastest. On the right the same readings are plotted against how many times each tray has dried out, over the fifty two dryings a weekly tray manages in a year, and the three drying lines land on top of one another. Spread apart on the left and stacked on the right means the drying is what wears the plant out rather than time. If both pictures looked the same, the plant would just be getting old and nightly drying would cost nothing.

how many times it has dried out
